answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through a stake-backed escrow: before a new identity can place orders, it locks a meaningful deposit, which is slashed if counterparties prove fraud through signed receipts and a dispute window. The kernel checks each claim against that identity’s history, while independent agents can challenge suspicious clusters. Splitting into many accounts then multiplies required capital and exposes each deposit to loss; a ledge or wharf of cheap aliases no longer buys cheap influence.
